paragraphs: Direct judgment: if you are willing to listen and respond steadily, record according to assessment and confidentiality standards, and escalate in a crisis, helping others improve their psychological and emotional health is a direction worth testing further. Safe trials use only completely fictional counseling cases and do not touch real client information or restricted data.

Observable signals: whether you can work according to the assessment and risk screening process, strictly follow confidentiality and record standards, and escalate immediately when a safety risk appears; personality labels cannot determine fit or qualification.

Suitable conditions: willing to handle emotional load and confidentiality responsibility over the long term, able to work steadily within supervision and license scope, and to keep learning. Caution conditions: if it is hard to bear a high emotional load and safety responsibility, first compare adjacent directions such as social services or psychological counseling.

A completely fictional paper package, 60 minutes, without touching real clients or information. A: an adult character, Lin, has just changed shifts and reports irregular sleep over the past two weeks and worry about work, and only wants to know the available support; no history, safety screening, consent scope, or diagnosis was provided. B: fictional institutional rules require learners to produce only a needs excerpt, a known/unknown list, and a handover draft; any safety clue goes first to a supervisor or qualified person according to institutional procedure, without independent assessment or handling. C: one sentence from a character was recorded as "sometimes feels like I cannot hold on", and its meaning and immediate safety status are unknown; the relatives ask for the full record but no disclosure authorization was given. Organize the facts and pending questions, two support goals to be confirmed by a professional, and a confidentiality/escalation handover and record template, without giving a diagnosis, treatment course, or danger level rating, and without uploading personal information to a tool.

entries: Assessment and planning: complete counseling needs assessment and risk screening, and develop a reviewable counseling and prevention plan.
Counseling and support: conduct individual or group counseling and prevention education, and keep records, referrals, and follow-up.

paragraphs: Mental health counselors correspond to O*NET 21-1014.00, whose duties are to provide counseling and advice to individuals and groups to promote optimal psychological and emotional health, with an emphasis on prevention; the work may help address addiction and substance use, family and marriage, stress management, self-esteem, and aging. This page does not equate counseling with diagnosis or mandatory intervention authority.

Work context (O*NET Work Context survey, 1—5 scale): characterized by intensive interpersonal contact, emotional load, and confidentiality requirements, with records kept according to assessment and safety standards; specific work context values follow the O*NET Work Context survey.

Abilities and work style: requires a foundation in counseling and assessment, the ability to strictly follow confidentiality and record standards, and escalation according to process when a crisis or safety risk appears.

Research inputs: the official description, tasks, work context, interest code (SI), and Job Zone Five of O*NET 21-1014.00, plus the BLS 2025 wages and the 2024—2034 employment projection (this occupation's framing); these are not used to infer qualifications, wages, or employment framing in mainland China.
Objects of work: individuals and groups facing issues such as addiction, family and marriage, stress, self-esteem, and aging, as well as referral sources and community resources.
Checkable outputs: counseling needs assessment and plan, counseling and prevention records, crisis handling and referral records, and follow-up and handover records.

Boundaries: this page describes the counseling, assessment, and prevention tasks of O*NET21-1014.00; the page itself does not grant diagnosis, prescribing, mandatory intervention, or independent practice authority, and specific professional duties and authorization must be confirmed by jurisdiction, license, and institution.

Adjacent relationships are used only for direction comparison: this occupation centers on counseling, assessment, and prevention, while clinical and counseling psychologists focus on psychological assessment and treatment, substance abuse counselors focus on addiction counseling, marriage and family therapists focus on family systems, rehabilitation counselors focus on disability and employment, and child, family, and school social workers focus on child and family services, and the qualifications and licenses of each position are not interchangeable.
When comparing, check item by item: who assesses, who treats, who has authority to handle a crisis, and who bears legal responsibility; similar names do not mean identical duties and authorization.

Difference from clinical and counseling psychologists: psychologists usually need a doctorate and a license and may conduct psychological assessment and treatment; this occupation's license and scope are verified by jurisdiction.
Difference from substance abuse counselors: the latter focus on addiction counseling; this occupation has a broader scope covering multiple mental health issues and prevention.

Difference from marriage and family therapists and rehabilitation counselors: the objects and specialties differ, and the specific authorization, supervision, and legal responsibility are verified by jurisdiction and license.

Use the fictional A/B/C package above to practice organizing facts and unknowns and handing over; tool prompts can only assist, cannot give a character a diagnosis or safety level, and must not upload real case information.

paragraphs: Fit signals: willing to listen and respond steadily, follow confidentiality and record standards, and escalate according to process when a crisis or safety risk appears. Caution conditions: if it is hard to bear a high emotional load and safety responsibility, first compare adjacent directions.

Use the fictional A/B/C package and reference deliverable above to practice only fact excerpts, unknowns, and handover drafts, with no diagnosis, safety grading, or real counseling. Paper performance is for exploration only, and real training, supervision, and licensing requirements must be checked separately.

Insufficient identification and handling of self-harm or harm-to-others risk: during assessment and counseling, triggered when the risk screening and escalation process is not followed; may endanger the client's or others' safety; control is to handle according to process and report immediately.

Improper handling of confidential information: during recording and communication, triggered when confidentiality and minimum necessity principles are not followed; may violate privacy regulations and damage trust; control is to handle according to the standards and keep records.

Providing counseling beyond license or authorization scope: during counseling, triggered when the scope is not confirmed according to license and supervision rules; may constitute a practice violation; control is to confirm the scope and refer.

Incomplete or inaccurate records: during recording, triggered when records are not written according to the record standards; affects continuity of service and traceability; control is to write according to the standards and review.

Common escalation rule: once a safety risk, confidentiality doubt, or out-of-scope request appears, pause the relevant step first and hand the facts, impact, and open questions to a supervisor or licensed person for confirmation before continuing.
This page collected no real recruitment samples; the following are position checks and editorial ability stages, not uniform hiring or qualification standards.

Position samples: grouped by community behavioral health agencies, hospitals and clinics, school and university counseling centers, private practice, and nonprofit organizations, checking the population, service model, scheduling, and licensing requirements.

BLS: U.S. mental health counselors usually need a master's degree and an internship, all states require licensure, and the specific examination and supervised clinical work requirements are checked by state; this is this occupation's requirement and is not derived from Job Zone Five. China checks requirements by the actual counseling/treatment category and institution.

Ability evidence: counseling experience is often evidenced by assessment, counseling plans, interventions, and supervision records, and must state the population, context, and results (de-identified).
Compliance requirements: confidentiality, informed consent, crisis handling, and mandatory reporting are verified against local law and licensing rules, which differ greatly across jurisdictions.

Works: the fact/unknown list for the fictional A/B/C above, a draft support goal, and a confidentiality and escalation handover record, marked as not touching real cases and not conducting diagnosis/screening or counseling. Seven days, 20 minutes a day: day 1 excerpt the known facts; day 2 list the unknown safety/consent/history items; day 3 write the questions to take to supervision and the timely escalation boundary; day 4 check the relatives' request and disclosure authority; day 5 organize the goals and a blank record; day 6 correct against the reference deliverable; day 7 compile the works, then check one target position's education/supervision/licensing requirements and record the source date, and record truthfully if not found. A real event with unknown safety must not wait for this paper learning plan.

Boundaries: degree, license, registration, and institutional authorization are not the same state; whether assessment, counseling, or crisis handling may be performed depends on the jurisdiction and license scope.

Ability ladder: before entering this occupation, check the official occupation scope, real employer requirements, education and licensing, local confidentiality and safety rules, and supervised tasks; advancement is based on reviewable assessment, counseling, and supervision records, not guaranteed years.

components.definition_block: Mental health counselors correspond to O*NET 21-1014.00, whose duties are to provide counseling and advice to individuals and groups to promote optimal psychological and emotional health, with an emphasis on prevention; the work may help address addiction and substance use, family and marriage, stress management, self-esteem, and aging.

fermat_decision_card.title: What kind of person is suited to being a mental health counselor?

fit_decision_checklist.how: A completely fictional paper package, 60 minutes, without touching real clients or information. A: an adult character, Lin, has just changed shifts and reports irregular sleep over the past two weeks and worry about work, and only wants to know the available support; no history, safety screening, consent scope, or diagnosis was provided. B: fictional institutional rules require learners to produce only a needs excerpt, a known/unknown list, and a handover draft; any safety clue goes first to a supervisor or qualified person according to institutional procedure, without independent assessment or handling. C: one sentence from a character was recorded as "sometimes feels like I cannot hold on", and its meaning and immediate safety status are unknown; the relatives ask for the full record but no disclosure authorization was given. Organize the facts and pending questions, two support goals to be confirmed by a professional, and a confidentiality/escalation handover and record template, without giving a diagnosis, treatment course, or danger level rating, and without uploading personal information to a tool. Reference deliverable: the known facts are only the shift change, two weeks of sleep difficulty, and a willingness to seek help; a diagnosis or a safe/unsafe judgment cannot be based on these. The meaning of "cannot hold on" and the immediate safety status are unknowns that must be promptly checked by a supervisor or qualified person according to institutional procedure and cannot wait for a routine weekly plan. The relatives' request has no disclosure authorization, so it goes first to the responsible person to verify under the applicable rules, and neither absolute confidentiality nor unilateral disclosure may be promised. The draft support goals may read "clarify available support resources" and "jointly determine reviewable goals with a professional", which is not a treatment prescription. The deliverable is a paper record with the original wording and time to be filled in, the unknowns, the handover recipient, and the items to be confirmed, without fabricating completed screening, signed consent, or actual counseling effects.
